**Today's computing stack straddles two world machines**

In [World Machines](https://worldmachines.org/theory) theory, Modernity, which pulls history toward one destination, is in its declining Dusk, and Divergence, where outcomes depend on local conditions, is in its Day. On our reading, digital computing's chips-and-scaling layer looks like late Modernity: frontier training costs up 2.4× a year, a concentrated chip supply. But energy is only 2–6% of that cost, and ordinary market economics explains the concentration just as well. The idea that AI's deployment belongs to Divergence has no support yet.

How sure: an untested idea, weakened by adversarial review. [The working analysis](https://github.com/msmsim/kinocomputing-lab/blob/main/analyses/a001-incumbent-stack-in-the-machines/ANALYSIS.md).
